title: Singers in the early bands
summary: Bands rarely hired singers; Williams recalls Harry Wells with Piron and singing by Pichon and Raymond Brown.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Did they have many bands that had singers? Oh, no. Uh-huh. They wouldn't hire singers if they were out?
No, no. Some of the guys in the band would holler, you know. But Varis Allen made about a thing. Varis Allen.
Who would do the singing in the band? Oh, different fellas. Sing.

Buddy never did sing. None of them didn't sing in the band. The only singer we hired was with Pierron, the boy named Harry Wells. We hired him when he was on the boat to sing with us. And I was with Pichon on the Pelican in 1928 and Raymond Brown and all of us. Pichon sang. Raymond would sing. What about Sam?
Did he sing any? Yeah, he'd sing that, yeah. I heard him on the record. I thought he could sing in person.
He'd sing whenever he'd get lonesome. Didn't he sing that on the record? No. Whenever he'd get lonesome, he just telephoned me.
How did he ever learn that?

Well, Ethel Waters recorded that. An okay record. Yeah, that's how he learned it. Was she ever down here? Yeah. There's an old Lyric Theater. We had a parking lot there in Burgundy and Iperville. That was the old Lyric. L-Y-R-I-C. Some people say Lyric. Well, it's Lyric. Yeah, Lyric. That's what we pronounce it, Creoles, I guess. That's right. L-Y-C-R-I-C, Lyric.
